description: We are STEM students from Alexandria, Egypt, aspiring to study computer science. We are interested in web development, programming, and AI, and we enjoy learning new technologies and building projects. We joined NASA Space Apps to challenge ourselves, explore space-related problems, collaborate as a team, and combine our skills to develop a creative and meaningful solution.
summary:
ExoLife is an interactive 3D space habitat simulation and mission-training web application built for Lunar and Martian exploration. Powered by React and Three.js, it enables multi-user crews to collaborate in real time across different devices using shared server rooms—executing retro-braking spacecraft landings, excavating multi-layer regolith strata, extracting mineral core samples, launching Earth sample-return capsules, and constructing modular outposts such as oxygen-producing Veggie Bio-Domes, water extractors, and solar arrays.

ExoLife directly addresses the challenge of sustaining long-term human survival in extreme off-world environments by modeling continuous, closed-loop life-support dynamics. Crews must actively monitor, troubleshoot, and balance depleting oxygen, water, power, food, radiation shielding, and astronaut health grounded in authentic NASA mission telemetry, while earning mission coins to unlock advanced tools and upgrade base infrastructure.

By transforming complex aerospace engineering, in-situ resource utilization (ISRU), and astrobiology concepts into an accessible, hands-on multiplayer experience, ExoLife bridges theoretical STEM education with practical mission operations—equipping and inspiring students, educators, and space enthusiasts for humanity's sustainable return to the Moon and future journey to Mars.
details:
ExoLife – Interactive 3D Space Habitat Simulation

ExoLife is an interactive 3D space habitat simulation and mission-training web application designed to explore the challenges of establishing sustainable human settlements on the Moon and Mars.

The project addresses one of the biggest challenges of future space exploration: How can humans survive and maintain a sustainable habitat in extreme environments where essential resources are limited and resupply from Earth is difficult?

How It Works

ExoLife transforms this challenge into an interactive simulation where users take on the role of space explorers responsible for operating and maintaining an extraterrestrial habitat.

Users can explore 3D Lunar and Martian environments, experience spacecraft landing scenarios, excavate different layers of regolith, investigate mineral formations, collect scientific samples, and construct modular habitat infrastructure.

A key feature of ExoLife is its real-time multiplayer system, which allows multiple crew members to connect and collaborate across different devices, sharing mission activities and working together toward common objectives.

The simulation also features a dynamic life-support and resource-management system. Oxygen, water, electricity, and food supplies are continuously affected by gameplay decisions and mission activities. Players must monitor these interconnected resources while considering radiation exposure and crew health. Poor resource management can affect habitat sustainability and mission success.

Additionally, ExoLife integrates working NASA APIs to retrieve real space-related data and connect the simulation with actual scientific resources. This helps bridge the gap between simulated mission operations and real-world space science.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ExoLife aims to make aerospace engineering and space science more accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts.

Its main benefits include:

  • Introducing users to the challenges of long-term human survival beyond Earth.
  • Demonstrating the importance of resource management and sustainable habitat design.
  • Explaining scientific concepts such as In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU).
  • Encouraging teamwork through real-time multiplayer mission collaboration.
  • Developing critical thinking, problem-solving, and systems engineering skills.
  • Connecting theoretical STEM knowledge with practical, interactive learning experiences.

Our intended impact is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and innovators by allowing them to explore the technologies and challenges associated with future Lunar and Martian missions.

Technologies and Development Tools

ExoLife was developed as a web-based application using modern frontend technologies.

Our technology stack includes:

  • React – Building the application interface and interactive components.
  • Three.js – Rendering immersive 3D environments.
  • Vite – Development and application building.
  • Tailwind CSS – Responsive interface styling.
  • React Router – Navigation between application sections.
  • JavaScript, HTML, and CSS – Application logic, structure, and presentation.
  • NASA Open APIs – Retrieving real space-related data and scientific information.
  • Real-time Multiplayer Technologies – Enabling synchronized collaboration between connected crew members.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes ExoLife different is the combination of space exploration, habitat construction, scientific investigation, dynamic resource management, and real-time multiplayer collaboration within one interactive experience.

Instead of presenting space science as static information, ExoLife allows users to actively participate in mission-related activities, make decisions, observe their consequences, and work with other crew members.

The project combines concepts from aerospace engineering, astrobiology, environmental systems, and ISRU to create an educational experience centered on the future of human exploration.

Design Considerations

During development, our team considered several important factors:

  • Scientific Relevance: Integrating NASA data and using real space exploration concepts as references.
  • Sustainability: Modeling resource limitations and the importance of maintaining balanced life-support systems.
  • Collaboration: Supporting real-time teamwork across multiple devices.
  • Accessibility: Making complex scientific concepts understandable through an interactive web-based experience.
  • User Experience: Designing an interface that makes exploration and mission activities engaging and easy to navigate.
  • Scalability: Building the application in a way that allows additional missions, environments, and simulation systems to be introduced.

Our Vision

ExoLife is more than a space exploration game. It is an educational simulation that brings together the engineering, scientific, and human challenges of living beyond Earth.

By combining real NASA data, interactive 3D environments, dynamic life-support systems, and collaborative gameplay, we hope to make the future of Lunar and Martian exploration something people can experience, understand, and imagine building themselves.

Explore. Survive. Build Beyond Earth. 🚀
